target_translation: base64.URLEncoding.DecodeString (padded), then parse the text as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' with an optional '.' and 1 to 6 fraction digits (what encode_cursor writes: naive, no offset). Return the time as UTC, which the Go DB codec writes as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.ffffff' for the < comparison. Invalid base64 or an unparsable text is an uncaught ValueError/binascii.Error in the original: 500. Return an error that the handler turns into a 500 and mark BUG(port): a bad ?cursor= gives 500. Python's b64decode also skips characters outside the alphabet; Go rejects them (TODO(port): only if a judge scenario sends one).
